summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 12% YoY to INR612 crore as volume dropped about 13% on a delayed monsoon; gross margin rose to 31.6%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations declined 12% YoY to INR612 crore from INR691 crore, with management attributing the drop to a delayed and uneven monsoon and high temperatures that pushed back crop protection demand. Gross profit fell 4% to INR193.16 crore, but gross margin widened from 29% to 31.6%, which management linked to premium mix and inventory effects amid volatile raw material prices. EBITDA margin fell from 12.2% to 11.1% and PAT margin from 8.4% to 7.2%. Management said the season was deferred rather than lost and expects stronger execution over the remaining three quarters, but declined to give revised FY27 targets until after H1.

financial_highlights.change: down from 12.2% YoY; EBITDA down about 20%
from INR97 crore YoY (lower Hachiman sales)
Products launched last year: INR2.29 crore vs INR1.67 crore YoY

segments.name: B2C (Q1 B2C product mix)
segments.commentary: Herbicide about 59%, insecticide about 33%, fungicide about 5%, PGR about 3% of B2C in Q1. Focus Maharatna and Maharatna portfolio about 64% of business.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Share rose to 34% of sales from 23% YoY; management said B2B grew more than B2C in Q1 and expects a similar pattern in Q2.

segments.name: Kaeros Research
segments.commentary: More than 40 products commercialised; management targets about 100% CAGR initially, normalised EBITDA margin in single digits at present.

segments.name: Granuvia and Spinoace (Corteva collaboration)
segments.commentary: Granuvia crossed about INR5 crore in Q1; Spinoace about INR25 lakh as launch was late July. Gross FY27 target INR30-35 crore combined, about INR25 crore net after 25% deduction.

guidance_outlook: Management expects herbicide sales to recover in Q2, with most herbicides expected to exceed last year's levels, but says dream FY27 herbicide targets will not be met.
Management expects positive sales impact from Q2 and says the first half (over 60% of annual sales) is critical; revised FY27 growth targets to be given after H1.
Management expects sales returns to fall to at least half of last year's level, with only one or two herbicides showing failures.
Management expects Q2 profitability to recover with sales expected after August; gross margin expected to hold as premium mix rises.
Management aims to double the company in 4-5 years, versus 3-4 years previously.
Once current projects complete, maintenance capex expected at INR30-40 crore per year.
Buyback or dividend to be decided after Q1; company historically buys back every 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Sotanala project: total about INR200 crore (INR50 crore formulation, INR150 crore technical); about INR70 crore invested to date. Formulation expected around April-May 2027, technical production by Diwali 2026, with 5-6 products in phase 1.
Dahej: about 50-60% of equipment utilised for the new plant; new power connection and a new boiler upcoming. Management sees at least INR200 crore of potential addition to technical production.
Chopanki expansion completed; Dahej more than 70% commercialised, with the remaining 20-30% expected soon.
Udhampur: investment to separate herbicide and insecticide plants, expected to complete within 2026.
IIL Crop Solutions: plots to be doubled from 36 to cover 14 states and 4 crops (rice, cotton, chilli, soybean).
Management expects to tighten power and steam costs through solar, wind and solid fuel, with benefits from end-Q2 onwards.
demand_pricing: Monsoon: delayed and uneven, with channel activity starting early in March. Management said August rains were good, but rice sowing lagged in South India (about 40% pending in Karnataka, Andhra and Tamil Nadu) and MP and some eastern states were dry.
Volume fell about 13% YoY in Q1, with value up about 2%, implying price/mix gains of about 2%.
Price hikes: one in March, two in April, and one attempted in May but rolled back as demand weakened; no significant price increase was realised through July.

Raw material pressure: solvent prices moved 25-30% week to week and some doubled; plastic, HDPE, emulsifiers and some technicals rose sharply, with freight and container scarcity worsening supply chains.
Management said inventory was slightly elevated in June and is expected to decline sharply in Q2 quarter.
Management said gross margin bands by product type: generics about 10-15% (up to 20-25% in some cases), Maharatna about 30% (20-25% in some), FM 35%+ (up to 40%+).

qa_highlights.question: Will sales returns recur as in last year (INR200 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects returns to fall to at least half of last year's level, citing lower placements, a variety of generic and new products, and only one or two herbicides failing.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q1 volume and value growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume fell about 13%, with value up about 2%.

qa_highlights.question: Kaeros growth and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 100% CAGR initially, moderating to 50-60%. Normalised margin is single-digit at present, and management does not expect it to reach double digits soon.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin expansion to 31.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 2% price rise, specialty product mix, and some benefit from older inventory, while noting volatile input prices. It said the net effect was mixed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sotanala investment and product plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Total about INR200 crore (INR50 crore formulation, INR150 crore technical); about INR70 crore spent to date. Phase 1 will transfer 5-6 existing insecticide and fungicide molecules from Chopanki; new AIs in phase 2.

qa_highlights.question: Granuvia and Spinoace revenue expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Granuvia crossed about INR5 crore in Q1; Spinoace INR25 lakh. Gross FY27 target INR30-35 crore combined, about INR25 crore net.

risks_watch: Q2 recovery hinges on delayed kharif demand; management says first half is over 60% of annual sales and will give revised FY27 targets only after H1.
Raw material volatility: solvent prices moved 25-30% week to week and some doubled; gross margin of 31.6% partly reflects older inventory, and management said the net effect was mixed.
Sales returns: management expects returns to fall to at least half of last year's INR200 crore, with only one or two herbicides showing failures; placements were kept lower this year.
Kaeros early-stage costs: about 100 people hired in Q1, normalised margin in single digits and not expected to reach double digits soon.
Pricing power: one hike in March, two in April, a May hike rolled back; no significant price increase realised through July.
Working capital: June inventory was slightly elevated and management expects a sharp decline in Q2; buyback or dividend to be decided after Q1.
key_quotes: So, I believe that the total turnover of the company dropped, so that was the reason there was impact in the profitability, which we should be able to recover in Q2 with improved sales number, which are expected after the August ends .
So, after that we'll review that what type of growth will be possible in this year and will give you revised targets.
I think that we should be able to reduce the sales return numbers to at least half what was there in the previous year.

Performance has been mixed with some progress well and some requiring sharper execution, better visibility now available on key drivers, area of opportunity, area of requiring corrective actions, need to move from initiatives to measurable outcomes is realized
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term growth (doubling in 4-5 years, premiumisation, Kaeros, Sotanala) but cautious on FY27, withholding revised targets until after H1 and saying Q1 was a setback. Answers were specific on Sotanala capex and the segment mix but evasive on brand-wise economics, Dahej returns and ROCE quantification.
